```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
```

TiffPlotR reads rectangular regions of large, multi-resolution (OME-)TIFF
images at a resolution suited to plotting, and returns them as tidy data plus
ggplot2 plots. This vignette uses the multiplex immunofluorescence image that
ships with the package.

```{r libraries}
library(TiffPlotR)
library(ggplot2)
# hide the per-fetch progress messages
options(TPR_VERBOSE = FALSE)
```

## The example image

```{r image-info}
tiff_path <- exampleTiff()
read_tiff_meta_data(tiff_path)
```

The image is 8651 x 5998 pixels at full resolution, with 6 channels and 5
resolution levels, each half the size of the one before. The OME-XML names and
colours each channel:

```{r channels}
read_tiff_channels(tiff_path)[, c("channel", "name", "color")]
```

## Fetching a region

`fetchTiffData()` reads a region, given as a `TiffRect` in full-resolution
pixel coordinates. It picks the coarsest resolution that keeps the plot at
least `max_pixels` (default 800) wide, so a large region is never read at full
resolution by accident.

```{r fetch}
rect <- TiffRect(xmin = 900, xmax = 2300, ymin = 1400, ymax = 2800)
img <- fetchTiffData(tiff_path, rect)
img
```

The result is a `TiffPlotData` object. `@data` holds one row per pixel and
channel, with raw `value`s and `norm_value`s scaled to 0-1 by each channel's
limits in `@precalc_max`. `@plots` holds the plots, and printing the object
draws the active plot. Opal 520 has no signal in this region, so its
normalized values are missing and its panel is grey.

```{r data}
head(img@data)
img@precalc_max
```

### Channel names

Channels are named by their OME names where the TIFF has them, and otherwise
`"channel 1"`, `"channel 2"`, and so on. `channel_names` can give your own
names, or `"number"` for bare channel numbers. `selected_channels` keeps a
subset, in the order given, by number or name:

```{r select}
fetchTiffData(tiff_path, rect,
              channel_names = c("nuclei", paste("marker", LETTERS[1:5])),
              selected_channels = c("marker D", "nuclei"))
```

## Composite images

`fetchTiffData.rgb()` shows three channels as red, green and blue.
`fetchTiffData.colorized()` blends any number of channels, each with its own
colour.

```{r rgb}
fetchTiffData.rgb(tiff_path, rect,
                  red_channel = "Opal 690", green_channel = "Autofluorescence",
                  blue_channel = "DAPI")
```

```{r colorized}
colorized <- fetchTiffData.colorized(tiff_path, rect,
                                     channel_colors = list(DAPI = "blue", "Opal 690" = "yellow"))
colorized
```

## Replotting without reading the image again

The `plotTiffData*()` functions build new plots from the data already in an
object. They return a ggplot, so they combine with any other ggplot2 code.

```{r replot}
plotTiffData(img, selected_channels = c("Opal 690", "DAPI"), ncol = 1,
             scale_colors = c("black", "white"))
```

```{r replot-composite}
plotTiffData.colorized(img, channel_colors = list(DAPI = "cyan", "Opal 690" = "magenta"))
```

With `return_object = TRUE`, the new plot is stored in the object instead and
becomes its active plot:

```{r replot-store}
img <- plotTiffData(img, value_var = "value", return_object = TRUE)
names(img@plots)
img@activePlot
```

## Adjusting contrast

`renormalize()` sets new limits for some channels and rebuilds the plots,
again without reading the image. Here the DAPI ceiling is lowered so dim
nuclei show up:

```{r renormalize}
bright <- renormalize(colorized, channels = "DAPI", max_value = 40)
bright
```

## Physical units

When the OME-XML records the pixel size, plots can be labelled in microns
instead of pixels and given a scale bar. Only the labels change: the data stay
in pixel coordinates, so shapes and zoom regions keep working.

```{r microns}
img <- fetchTiffData(tiff_path, rect, selected_channels = c("DAPI", "Opal 690"),
                     um_axes = TRUE, scale_bar = TRUE)
img
```

`set_axes_um()`, `set_axes_pixel()` and `add_um_scale_bar()` do the same for
an existing plot or object.

## Zooming in

Shapes such as `TiffRect` can be drawn on a plot with `shape_annotate()`, and
then fetched in more detail. Passing the overview's `precalc_max` keeps the
contrast the same in both.

```{r zoom-overview}
zoom <- TiffRect(xmin = 1500, xmax = 1800, ymin = 2100, ymax = 2400)
overview <- fetchTiffData.colorized(tiff_path, rect,
                                    channel_colors = list(DAPI = "blue", "Opal 690" = "yellow"))
shape_annotate(overview, zoom, color = "white", fill = NA)
```

```{r zoom-detail}
fetchTiffData.colorized(tiff_path, zoom, precalc_max = overview@precalc_max,
                        channel_colors = list(DAPI = "blue", "Opal 690" = "yellow"))
```

The zoomed region is small enough to be read at full resolution.

## Adding points

`add_points()` overlays point data, such as cell centroids from a segmentation
tool, on a composite plot without losing its channel legend. As a stand-in for
real per-cell results, this takes bright DAPI pixels and calls them positive
when Opal 690 is also high:

```{r points}
d <- overview@data
dapi <- d[d$channel_name == "DAPI" & d$norm_value > 0.5, c("i", "j")]
opal <- d[d$channel_name == "Opal 690", c("i", "j", "norm_value")]
cells <- merge(dapi, opal, by = c("i", "j"))
cells <- cells[seq(1, nrow(cells), by = 25), ]
cells$status <- ifelse(cells$norm_value > 0.4, "positive", "negative")

add_points(overview@plots$colorized, cells, x = "i", y = "j", colour_by = "status",
           palette = c(positive = "red", negative = "white"), size = 1)
```

## Package options

Options set the defaults for every fetch, for example in `.Rprofile`. Each
object records the settings it was made with in `@plot_parameters`, and
`plotTiffData*()` reuses them. See `?TiffPlotR` for the full list.

```{r options}
options(TPR_MAX_PIXELS = 400,
        TPR_UM_AXES = TRUE,
        TPR_UM_SCALE_BAR = TRUE,
        TPR_SCALE_BAR_STYLE = list(line_color = "yellow", position = "bottomright"),
        TPR_THEME = theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black"),
                          panel.grid = element_blank()))
img <- fetchTiffData(tiff_path, rect, selected_channels = c("DAPI", "Opal 570", "Opal 690"))
img
str(img@plot_parameters[c("max_pixels", "um_axes", "scale_bar", "scale_bar_style")])
```

```{r options-reset}
options(TPR_MAX_PIXELS = NULL, TPR_UM_AXES = NULL, TPR_UM_SCALE_BAR = NULL,
        TPR_SCALE_BAR_STYLE = NULL, TPR_THEME = NULL)
```

## Saved objects

`TiffPlotData` objects can be saved with `saveRDS()`. Objects saved by older
versions of TiffPlotR are updated automatically when used, with a warning;
`update_TiffPlotData()` updates one explicitly so it can be saved again.
